_register: Formal, polite address: instructions in sentences use the 2nd person plural imperative (Επιλέξτε, Σαρώστε τον γραμμωτό κώδικα, Περιμένετε), never the informal singular (επίλεξε); buttons and menu entries use the noun of the action or the short polite imperative (Δανεισμός, Αποθήκευση, Εκτύπωση); no jokes, no exclamation marks; modern monotonic Greek only.
_quotes: Greek guillemets «text» with no space inside them (e.g. «{{title}}»); nested quotes use “ ”; the Greek question mark is the semicolon (;) written right after the last word with no space before it, the ano teleia (·) is not used in the interface; the colon and other punctuation take no space before them; decimals use the comma and thousands the dot as in Greece, but numbers come from placeholders; the arrow → stays.
_plural: Two forms (one, other); the definite article, the adjective and the verb agree in gender, number and case with the noun, so a plural message should hold the whole phrase in each option (e.g. {{count:plural; one:1 αντίτυπο; other:{{count}} αντίτυπα;}}), because the noun's case changes with the sentence.

copy.note: One physical copy with its own barcode; plural «αντίτυπα». Never «αντίγραφο», which means a duplicate or backup.

record.note: Catalogue entry of a title (βιβλιογραφική εγγραφή in full); «εγγραφή» alone is used in menus and messages, and is distinct from the verb «εγγραφή μέλους».

patron.note: Usual word in Greek school libraries; feminine «αναγνώστρια» only where the gender is known, otherwise the masculine plain form. Koha says «δανειζόμενος», which is longer and describes only the act of borrowing.

card.note: Short form «κάρτα» where the context is clear.

loan.note: The action and the area of the program; one loan as an item is also «δανεισμός».

return.note: The action: «Επιστροφή» on the menu; the verb is «επιστρέφω» / «καταχωρίστε την επιστροφή».

renew.note: Extending the due date; verb «ανανεώνω». «Παράταση» is also used but «ανανέωση» is the word of library systems (Koha), so keep it everywhere.

overdue.note: Adjective form «εκπρόθεσμος» is avoided in labels as it is heavier; use «σε καθυστέρηση» (the loan is in delay).

reminder.note: The printed slip asking for the return.

call number.note: The shelf mark on the spine (B 4 DEL, 590 ROS), the word used in Greek libraries for the shelving number.

spine band.note: The coloured band with pictogram and call number on the spine; kept distinct from «ετικέτα» (label).

barcode.note: The standard Greek term; plural «γραμμωτοί κώδικες». «Barcode» in Latin letters is not used in the interface.

class.note: A school class such as «Γ΄ Β» that patrons belong to (the section); «τάξη» means the year level (grade) and is used only for that.

group.note: Used for a group of teachers.

genre.note: Literary genre; «λογοτεχνικό είδος» in full text.

classification.note: The sorting scheme (Dewey decimal for non-fiction: «Δεκαδική Ταξινόμηση Dewey»).

stocktaking.note: Checking the shelves against the catalogue; the usual word for library inventory checks in Greece.

wish list.note: Books a patron would like the library to have; «λίστα επιθυμιών» sounds like a shop and is not used.

census.note: Registering the patrons with their photo; short form «καταγραφή».

class upgrade.note: Moving every class up a year at the end of the school year; «προαγωγή» is the school word for promotion to the next year.

anonymise.note: Verb «ανωνυμοποιώ»; erase the personal data for good.

backup.note: Plural «αντίγραφα ασφαλείας»; do not confuse with «αντίτυπο» (a copy of a book).

scanner.note: The USB barcode reader that types like a keyboard; short form «σαρωτής» in labels and in text when the context is clear.

student.note: Feminine «μαθήτρια» only where the gender is known; plural «μαθητές» covers both.

teacher.note: Gender-neutral official word in Greek schools; do not use «δάσκαλος/καθηγητής», which depend on the school level.

configuration.note: Plural noun for a settings area; the singular «διαμόρφωση» is used for the act of configuring.

return desk / circulation desk.note: The desk where loans and returns are handled; the area as a whole is «Δανεισμός».
